reviewedInvariants.area: Native timeout admission and effect closure
reviewedInvariants.evidence: LegadoHostEffectRecorder.record and close share one NSLock. Native timeout closes effect admission before cancelling pending and before returning its timeout response. OriginalWebCookieIPCWait.beginIssue invokes the throwing admission immediately before the actual synchronous WebKit issue call. A sealed request denies admission; an already admitted call is conservatively included even if cancellation arrives before its asynchronous completion. Denied old children cannot issue their first unreported mutation.

OriginalWebCookieIPCWait owns one continuation and first Result under its separate NSLock. install handles an early cancellation result; finish publishes only the first result and clears the continuation. Cancellation before beginIssue prevents issuance, cancellation during/after admission resumes the waiter once, and a late WebKit callback becomes a no-op. No main-thread semaphore is introduced. The native JNI worker semaphore remains explicitly off-main.

Cookie clear/response/text use clearly named MayCommit claims before entering the possibly noninterruptible actor/file commit. Real success records separate acknowledgement facts. WK records mutation issuance immediately before actual platform invocation and completion-stage facts afterward. Timeout responses retain conservative admission/issued facts rather than declaring rollback or a completed file write. Host/JVM error metadata does not upgrade the possibility into full Cookie/native acceptance.

Host validates the existing binding/revision and the actual absolute request deadline. Existing pendingEntityOperations tickets cover Cookie operations; task cancel cancels those tickets. WebKit pending tasks are additionally tracked by task/owner and cancelled on task cancellation, owner revoke and source revision replacement. Cookie planning, each IPC boundary and final actor publication check task cancellation, the binding cancellation ticket, operation ticket and the same actor observation revision.

Original CookieDao.deleteOkHttp SQL deletes only keys containing literal ASCII pipe. clearOriginalOkHttp removes only such legacyHeaders/originalRawDomains rows in the existing file and leaves originalMemoryText, rich native Cookies and WK store intact. Therefore new RuntimeSession/Host bindings share cached original Cookie/session text; only a genuinely fresh Cookie owner/process starts with remaining persisted rows.

reviewedInvariants.area: Original remove and WebKit target scope
reviewedInvariants.evidence: AppCookieOwnerClient.mutate performs the existing DB/cache remove and requires its acknowledgement before webRemove. webRemove sends exactly original NetworkUtils.getDomain/getSubDomain targets. The native operation expires root-path names at those exact targets, re-observes between targets and leaves other paths/domains alone. It uses an expiration setter rather than broadly deleting a possibly separate .domain Cookie with unknown hostOnly provenance.

The operation uses WKWebsiteDataStore.default().httpCookieStore in production, with an explicitly injected actual nonpersistent store only in native fixtures. It creates no WKWebView, navigation lease, JSContext, new queue, replacement jar or HTTP transport. The final observed snapshot returns to the same CookiePersistenceOwner; authoritative controlled identities do not rewrite original raw DB/cache text or guessed hostOnly/origin metadata.

CookiePersistenceOwner.accept validates before planning and again after its beforeWrite hook, replaces the file before publishing document/native/cache values, and skips unchanged writes. Browser IPC cannot be undone on later persistence failure/cancel/revoke, so the error retains those effects and the stale actor snapshot cannot be acknowledged. This is Foundation atomic replacement, not explicit fsync or power-loss proof.
